> "You may ask us to waive collection if the overpayment was not your fault and you cannot afford to pay it back. There is no time limit to ask for a waiver."

A **waiver**, which means asking them to drop the money so you do not have to pay it back. The letter says you can ask for this if two things are true: the overpayment was not your fault, *and* you do not have enough money to pay it back.

What is the difference between the 'waiver' and the 'appeal'? They sound the same to me.

So an appeal is for when you believe you were not overpaid, or that $1,284.00 is not the right amount. Maybe your pay from work was not what they say. Maybe the months are wrong. You are asking them to check their own work again.

**The waiver is about paying it back.**

With a waiver, you are not arguing about $1,284.00. You are saying two other things: the mistake was not yours, and you do not have the money to return it.

> "If you do nothing, we will withhold $73.00 from your monthly payment starting January 2027."

- **They take the money themselves.** You do not send a payment. They keep part of what they would have paid you.
- **The amount is $73.00.** That comes out of each monthly payment.
